details: Hopes for an extension of US-Iran peace talks are easing geopolitical tensions, leading to a "risk-on" sentiment across global markets. This optimism has contributed to a rally in cryptocurrencies, with Bitcoin hovering around $74,500 and other digital assets also seeing gains. Direct negotiations between US and Iranian officials reportedly commenced on April 15, marking a significant diplomatic shift from previous mediated discussions. While initial talks are preliminary and require more time, markets have already begun pricing in a positive outcome.
title: US-Iran Peace Talk Hopes Drive Risk-On Sentiment, Boosting Crypto

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has downgraded its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% from 3.3%, primarily due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The IMF warns of a potential global recession if the US-Iran conflict intensifies and oil prices remain above $100 per barrel through 2027. Furthermore, the IMF projects that global public debt could approach 100% of the world's GDP by 2029, raising concerns about fiscal stability and potentially bolstering the long-term case for Bitcoin as a hedge against traditional financial instability.
title: IMF Warns of Global Debt Surge, Potential Recession Amid Mideast Conflict

details: Grinex, a cryptocurrency exchange with strong ties to Russia and assessed as a successor to the sanctioned Garantex, has suspended all operations following an alleged "large-scale cyberattack." The exchange claims over 1 billion rubles (approximately $13.1 million) in user funds were stolen, attributing the breach to "special services of unfriendly states." The stolen assets were reportedly converted into TRX and consolidated into a single wallet, raising renewed concerns about exchange security risks and sanctions evasion structures within the crypto market.
title: Sanctioned Russia-Linked Crypto Exchange Grinex Halts Operations After $13M Hack
